note: Planning only: predicts the gas of one native-lane ILedger.execute publication from its actions, so the SDK can split a large write into publications without an eth_estimateGas round trip per guess. eth_estimateGas stays the authority before sending. Excluded: the 21,000 intrinsic cost and calldata (EIP-2028/7623; computable from the encoded transaction), refunds (EIP-3529; not applied, so the model errs high on clears), the signed lane, guards and STAGE/COMMIT.

method.amsterdam: FOUNDRY_PROFILE=amsterdam FOUNDRY_OUT=out/amsterdam FOUNDRY_CACHE_PATH=cache/amsterdam (solc experimental amsterdam target; never release bytes)
method.measurement: vm.lastFrameGas() of the execute call frame (gasTotalUsed, and gasStateUsed under amsterdam); every account the setUp touched is cooled (vm.cool) before each measured execute, so each publication pays the cold costs of a transaction of its own; the principal has written before except in the first-write pair
method.marginal: cost of one action = gas(k = 2) − gas(k = 1) of two publications of the same shape with distinct bodies
method.slopes: perWord and perByte: least squares of the files-bytes/1 marginal over body sizes 64, 100, 1000, 1024, 4096, 8192 (100 and 1,000 are not word multiples, which separates the two terms); publishNew[shape] = its marginal − perWord·ceil(n/32) − perByte·n, averaged over the measured sizes (fit.publishNewBaseBySize)
method.fixed: median of 2·gas(k = 1) − gas(k = 2) over the anchor pairs only (fit.fixedAnchors: the pairs the model had at 899767e, frozen in tools/gas-fit.mjs), so a row added later never changes the price of an existing action; fit.impliedFixedByPair keeps the value of every pair, anchors or not (the first action of a kind in a publication pays some cold state that later ones find warm, which this single constant averages)
method.firstWriteSurcharge: (CREATE + PUBLISH files-directory/1 as a principal's first publication ever) − (the same shape by a principal that has written once)
method.keys: PUBLISH new: publishNew[shape] + perWord·ceil(n/32) + perByte·n, n = body bytes; FOLDER binds run FilesFinalValidator; rebind = CAS to a new target; UNBIND/RELEASE from BOUND; restore = BIND from MASKED to the kept target; PROPERTY binds are a label (labelKey("en") on a word page → an existing text/1; a label with a new text is publishNew["text/1"] + its body terms + bindPropertyFresh, validated by "validate label new text"); SAME and BROADER first statements run FilesFinalValidator's topic checks on subject and role (word page to word page; bindSameFreshPath 2-word path to path), their later statements are on word pages; WITHDRAW of one occurrence
method.tagLevels: a first TAG statement (either sign) on an n-word topic = bindTagFresh (no author has stated anything at the position) or bindTagSecondAuthor (the position exists; measured as a first yes, which files one place entry, so it is an upper bound for a first no there) + Σ over its n − 1 proper ancestors of tagLevel.mineNew | mineExisting (the author's scope-below list at that ancestor is empty | not) + (a fresh position, either sign, or a first yes at an existing position: every filing) tagLevel.sharedNew | sharedExisting (the place-below list at that ancestor is empty | not); a list with exactly 1 entry or a multiple of 5 takes a fresh word on its next append, so price it as new (tagLists.priceAsNew). Measured: (k2 − k1) / 4 of a first statement on a 2-word and on a 6-word topic from the same state (rows "tag level all new | all existing": a first tag at a fresh position; "mine new | mine existing": a first no at an existing position, which files nothing below); shared = all − mine
method.laterLists: later statements are priced by laterLists (the list tiers); the tier rows are their own k1/k2 pairs (GasModel.t.sol section 9: `<row> new place` at three places whose lists hold one entry; `<row> long new place` at three places whose lists hold 1,025 entries, each statement at entry 1,024; `<row> long same place` at one place of 1,025 entries, k1 the entry at 512, k2 those at 256 and 768), never anchors, so no tier row moves `fixed` or an existing row; PROPERTY, SAME and BROADER rows are already measured at distinct subjects, so they carry no `NewPlace` row
method.maxima: maxAbsErrorPercent, maxUnderErrorPercent (and on amsterdam maxAbsExecutionErrorPercent, maxUnderExecutionErrorPercent) are taken over every validation composite whose state is not in maximaExcludeStates (beyondClaim: lists over laterLists.claimEntries, the floor's documented exception), and tools/gas-model.mjs refuses a model in which any of them exceeds 15%; the excluded composites are listed with their errors

planning.rule: A publication is planned when it is inside limits (1 ≤ actions ≤ maxActions, bind-kind actions ≤ maxBindsPerPublication, PUBLISH body bytes ≤ maxBodyBytesPerPublication) and max(E, V) ≤ floor(txGasCap × (100 − headroomPercent) / 100), on the schedule of the chain: E the model's execution estimate (prague: constants; amsterdam: split.executionGas), V the floor's visible-gas requirement (profiles.<schedule>.floor.formula). A shape that does not fit is split into publications before it is signed, never shortened; eth_estimateGas on the exact call stays the authority before sending, and the gas limit comes from the estimate, never from V.
planning.txGasCapRule: EIP-7825 (on amsterdam, EIP-8037: the cap counts execution gas only)
planning.headroomCovers: the 21,000 intrinsic cost, calldata (EIP-2028/7623) and the model's own error over the validation composites in both states (the author's lists new and existing). The cap condition is tested against the under-prediction of the gas the cap counts (headroom exists to stop a plan coming out too small; an over-prediction only costs batch size): on prague all gas, profiles.prague.maxUnderErrorPercent; on amsterdam execution gas only, profiles.amsterdam.maxUnderExecutionErrorPercent. The maximum-error fields keep their meaning (maxAbsErrorPercent, and on amsterdam maxAbsExecutionErrorPercent); profiles.amsterdam.maxAbsErrorPercent is the all-gas error (execution + state gas), which bounds the publication's total against the block, never the 2^24 cap. Each figure names its composite (maxAbsErrorComposite, maxUnderErrorComposite, maxAbsExecutionErrorComposite, maxUnderExecutionErrorComposite), each is taken over the composites whose state is not in maximaExcludeStates, and each is at most headroomPercent

tagLists.note: A per-author (scope-below) or shared (place-below) roll-up list holding exactly one entry, or a multiple of five entries (zero included: an empty list), takes a fresh word on its next append, so price that append as new (tagLevel.mineNew or sharedNew); otherwise as existing. The fresh word costs one slot rewrite more than a new list, inside the headroom; not separately measured.

laterLists.rule: A LATER statement (a planner bind action with first false: a mask, release, restore or re-bind) is priced by its place and the author's entry count there. Its place is (purpose, subject): the author's scope list keyed by (author, purpose, subject), which holds one entry per position the author has ever stated at that subject (masked and released ones included); `entries` is that list's length (IBitmapStore.scopeHead(Keys.scope(author, purpose, subject)).count, as TopicLookupReader.entryCount(author, purpose, place, false, …) returns it). `firstAtPlace` is true when no earlier later statement of the same publication is at the same place, of any kind. Short tier (entries known and ≤ shortTierMaxEntries): the row, or <row>NewPlace for the first later statement at its place when the constants carry one. Long tier (entries > shortTierMaxEntries, or unknown): <row>LongNewPlace when first at its place, else <row>LongSamePlace, measured at entry 1,024 of a 1,025-entry list (claimEntries). A row with no <row>LongNewPlace (a re-bind: a BIND on a BOUND head, which never searches the list) has no tier: <row>NewPlace when first at its place and the constants carry one, else the row.
laterLists.note: Cost depends on the list's length (RealmIndex._entryIndex bisects it, one store call per probe) and on the changed entry's index (an entry from 48 up has its live bit in a word of its own); a list of at most 48 entries bounds both. A count lower than the truth (a stale read) puts a long list in the short tier and under-prices it, so treat a count older than what the planner trusts as unknown. Above claimEntries the long tier is still applied but is outside what the stated maxima cover (state beyondClaim), as the floor's documented exception is.

floor.formula: The kernel's quote (LedgerIngress._foldAndQuote, work-model formula 3, docs/WORK-MODEL-V3.md) over a publication of n actions: fresh10 = workModel.freshPerPublication + Σ over PUBLISH/REUSE (freshPerRef·types[T].refs, plus freshPerPublishFresh + freshPerDigestSpec·types[T].specs when the record is new, or freshPerPublishExisting when it exists: a repeat PUBLISH or any REUSE) + Σ over rows (fresh); rw10 = rwPerPublication + rwPerPublish per PUBLISH/REUSE + Σ over rows (rw); compute = computeBase + n·computePerAction + Σ over rows (compute). Each BIND/UNBIND/RELEASE adds one row by class: (freshPerBindFirst, rwPerBindFirst, computePerBindFirst) for a first statement (a BIND or UNBIND whose author's head at the position is UNSET), (freshPerRebind, rwPerRebind, computePerRebind) for a re-bind (a BIND on a BOUND head: a new target, or the same target with a new number), and (freshPerBindLater, rwPerBindLater, computePerBindLater) for every other later statement (a mask, a release, a restore; a RELEASE always); when its purpose word equals surchargePurpose (never when it is zero) the surcharge row of the same class is added too (surchargeFreshFirst, surchargeRwFirst, surchargeComputeFirst; surchargeFreshRebind, surchargeRwRebind, surchargeComputeRebind; surchargeFreshLater, surchargeRwLater, surchargeComputeLater). Every WITHDRAW after the first of a publication adds the later-statement row (without the surcharge). With no principal (indexFloor) every bind-kind action adds the largest of the three rows field by field, surcharge included. freshSlots = ceil(fresh10 / 10), rewrites = ceil(rw10 / 10). The kernel refuses a work model whose reply is not 32 words or whose formulaVersion is not 3 (E_WORK_MODEL). prefixFloor P = compute + freshSlots·limits.floorFreshGas + rewrites·limits.floorRewriteGas; finalReserve F = finalComputeBase + binds·finalComputePerBind + publishes·finalComputePerPublish (binds = the BIND/UNBIND/RELEASE count, publishes = the PUBLISH/REUSE count). The checks (design §6.4, §6.5): before callback i the kernel requires its gasleft g > F + T and forwards (g − F − T)·63/64 to the ingress, which spends at most dispatchOverhead, then requires (its gasleft)·63/64 ≥ R_i = max(0, P − the callbacks' spend so far) (E_INDEX_GAS otherwise); before the final phase it requires (g − T)·63/64 ≥ F. T = limits.kernelTail. Sufficient visible execution gas (G = the gas limit less intrinsic gas and calldata): G ≥ V = max(K + ceil((ceil(P·64/63) + dispatchOverhead)·64/63), E) + ceil(F·64/63) + T, where E is the publication's execution gas and K the kernel's own share of it (callbacks excluded): at callback i the gas spent so far is at most K plus the callbacks' spend s, and R_i·(64/63)² ≥ P·(64/63)² − s, so the kernel's spend and the floor never need more than K + P·(64/63)²; the final check needs at most E + F·64/63 + T. A planner uses the model's execution estimate for E (prague: constants; amsterdam: split.executionGas) and floor.kernel (the same model fitted with the callbacks removed) for K. ILedgerCommitments.indexFloor quotes without a principal, so it prices every bind-kind action with the largest of the three rows field by field: it is an upper bound on P only, and a consumer plans from this rule, never from indexFloor.
floor.quantity: execution gas visible to the GAS opcode (on amsterdam the EIP-8037 state-gas reservoir is not visible and the cap counts execution gas only)

reads.note: Planning only: what one cold topic-reader view call costs (no intrinsic, no calldata) and the bounds that keep one call under callGasCap. Per-row terms are the same on both schedules (reads are not repriced); amsterdam's openings carry about 4k more of cold accounts. The below views' viewed-place check reads only head states (one word per head) and skips what cannot be MASKED: a lens author whose exact scope list at the place is all live (mine) and, with at least 4 lens authors to ask, a viewed position nobody ever stated anything at (both views); mineBelow and everyoneBelow are fitted where those shortcuts never apply (the bounds), mineBelowQuiet and everyoneBelowQuiet where they always do. A skipped entry of `everyone` (nobody says yes) reads its cell and its author-list head and no lens, so its cost does not grow with the lens (it was 49k at a lens of 1, 357k at 64 exact and 1.56M at 64 below when the lens was read first).

method.measurement: one cold view call per row of the suite: vm.cool on every account the call can touch, then vm.lastCallGas().gasTotalUsed
method.mine: gas = opening + openingPerLensAuthor·L + Σ over rows (perRow + perLensIndex·(j + 1)), j the deciding lens index; least squares over lens 1, 8, 32, 64 and pages 10, 50 of the round-robin fixture (mineExact: filed at the place; mineBelow: the worst case under a descendant, a statement at every viewed position and a masked entry in every lens author's exact list at the place, so every row reads the head states of lens[0..j] at the viewed place; mineBelowQuiet: under a descendant with nothing stated at the place, so no viewed-place head is read); negative terms clamped to 0
method.everyone: gas = opening + Σ over rows (perRow + perLensAuthor·L) + Σ over skipped entries perSkippedEntry; perRow and opening from raw (no lens), perLensAuthor from the lens-8 page (every lens head read: no lens author has a stance; below, everyoneBelow from the worst case with a statement at every viewed position, everyoneBelowQuiet with none), perSkippedEntryByLens from a padded place (lone negatives, lens 1, 8 and 64)
method.bounds: budget = callGasCap × (100 − marginPercent) / 100; maxRows = floor((budget − opening(L)) / worst row(L)), the worst row decided by the last lens author (j + 1 = L); maxSkippedEntries = floor((budget − opening) / the largest perSkippedEntry); a page that mixes both stays under budget while opening + rows·row(L) + skipped·perSkippedEntry ≤ budget
method.recommended: pageTimesLens: the smallest maxRows·L over lens 8..64 per view (keep maxRows·L at or below it); maxRows: at most 150 rows per call; limitEntries: the most entries one `everyone` call reads when none is a row, at a lens of 64
